summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Nebula GPU Systems. Main topics: Nebula exploring bundling Redwood inference as managed offering on top of their GPU fleet, verifying compatibility with Nebula GPU SKUs, private/VPC deployment options, and go-to-market co-sell model. Agreed next step: Redwood to share architecture doc and pricing; schedule technical deep-dive to scope pilot.
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-28 16:00 UTC; Duration ~48m; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Partnerships); Evan (Nebula Partnerships), Dr. Sana Iqbal (CTO), Marco (Solutions Arch)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, with Luis our SE and Priya on partnerships. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Evan: Good thanks, excited to chat. We sent over a short agenda: partner intro, technical compatibility, and GTM ideas.
[00:18] Luis: Awesome, I'll cover the infra compat questions — mostly around model sizes, quantization, and how our Private/Dedicated options map to your fleet.
[00:26] Dr. Sana: Great, I'll jump in on the hardware side — Nebula runs mixed clusters, A100s and a new Ampere-derived board we're testing. Latency matters, but we also want to understand throughput economics.
[00:38] Maya: Makes sense. High level, Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployments for partners. For OEM/partner integrations the common patterns are: 1) co-managed hosted where you resell access, 2) Dedicated capacity on your infra with Redwood control plane, or 3) full Private (VPC/on-prem) where you run the runtime and we provide ops tooling.
[00:58] Marco: Quick clarifier — with Dedicated, can you run on our hardware or is it hosted by Redwood?
[01:04] Luis: Dedicated can be colocated on partner infra. There are a few flavors: we can run the Redwood runtime in your cluster with routing and control-plane hooks back to Redwood, or we can provide the runtime as a containerized appliance that you manage. Network requirements are standard — VPC peering, gRPC endpoints, NAT rules.
[01:20] Dr. Sana: And for model compatibility, what's the supported quantization and kernel sets? We build custom kernels sometimes.
[01:28] Luis: We support INT8/4 quantization paths and have kernel selection per architecture. There are occasional perf regressions on non-standard kernels; we'd want to run a quick benchmark on your Ampere board. We can ship a small perf harness.
[01:42] Evan: That would be great. From GTM, Nebula wants to offer a managed Redwood endpoint bundled with our GPU fleet to enterprise customers — we handle the infra, you provide the inference runtime and billing?
[01:52] Maya: Exactly, that's a common model. We can do white-label endpoints and co-billing. There are legal/ops things — reseller terms, SLA alignment, and telemetry to surface usage for revenue sharing.
[02:03] Priya: On co-sell, we usually start with a pilot: define success metrics (latency P50/P95, throughput, cost per token), a short PO for reserved capacity and a pilot scope for 30–90 days.
[02:16] Dr. Sana: Security: can you outline KMS integration and audit logs? We need SOC2 and customer-managed keys for some clients.
[02:24] Luis: We integrate with cloud KMS and HSMs; Private deployments support customer KMS. We also surface audit logs, RBAC, and per-tenant telemetry. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:36] Marco: Any blockers for network—latency between our rack and Redwood control plane?
[02:41] Luis: For control plane it's fine — typical heartbeat and tracing are small. For data plane traffic we prefer local egress — in dedicated/on-prem mode data stays in your network; Hosted mode will obviously go over the public internet unless you use a VPN or VPC peering.
[02:56] Evan: Pricing — high level do you do fixed per-GPU host fees or per-token pricing?
[03:01] Maya: For partners we can mix models: for bundled offerings partners often do reserved monthly capacity (hosted or dedicated) plus per-token adjustments for overage. We'll share partner pricing tiers.
[03:12] Dr. Sana: For our customers, predictable cost is important, so reserved capacity makes sense. Also, ability to pin model versions and rollbacks matter for compliance.
[03:23] Luis: We support model pinning and rollout policies (canary/A-B and automatic fallback). That should cover regulatory/control needs.
[03:33] Evan: Any reference partners doing similar?
[03:36] Priya: We have a couple — not public — but examples include cloud partners bundling Dedicated and ISV partnerships. We'll share case studies.
[03:45] [small crosstalk]
[03:50] Marco: On the technical side, what telemetry do we need to provide to run the perf harness? We can expose perf counters and nvml metrics.
[03:58] Luis: NVML metrics are perfect. We'll need model names, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and expected QPS. We'll send a perf harness repo link — should take an hour to run basic samples.
[04:12] Dr. Sana: For quantization testing, do you prefer example models or our own fine-tuned models?
[04:18] Luis: Start with a representative open model (e.g., Llama2 variant) then run your fine-tuned models. The main goal is to validate kernel paths and memory footprint.
[04:29] Maya: On legal, we typically require a reseller addendum and an MOU for pilot. Pricing and SLA specifics come after initial perf validation.
[04:39] Evan: Timeline — Nebula wants to launch an MVP integration by Q1 2026 if possible. Is that feasible?
[04:46] Maya: Feasible. Typical flow: perf validation (1–2 weeks), pilot setup (2–6 weeks depending on infra), then go-to-market prep. So Q1 aligns if we start soon.
[04:58] Priya: We'll prepare a partner one-pager with co-sell models and sample revenue splits.
[05:04] Marco: One more thing — are there any hard restrictions on GPU drivers or hypervisor? We use a custom driver stack for our Ampere-derived board.
[05:12] Luis: We'll need to validate drivers. Sometimes custom stacks require kernel-level tuning; our SEs have worked with partners to adapt. We'll note that as a risk and schedule the deep-dive.
[05:23] [pause]
[05:25] Maya: Great. Recap of agreed next steps: Redwood sends partner one-pager, security pack, and perf harness. Nebula shares expected QPS and GPU details. Schedule technical deep-dive next week.
[05:40] Evan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:44] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR noise — names sometimes garbled; timestamps approximate.
